description: The bar chart titled “Average performance on November 2024 AMC 10/12 tests” visually compares the average scores of various language models on math competitions, with scores normalized such that a score of 0.5 corresponds to random guessing, and higher scores indicate better performance. The vertical axis, labeled “Average score (temperature = 0.5),” ranges from 60 to 90 in increments of 10, and each bar is annotated with its exact score. The horizontal axis lists 10 models: Llama 3.1 70B, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Qwen 2.5 14B-Instruct, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen 2.5 72B-Instruct, Gemini Flash 1.5, Gemini Pro 1.5, and phi-4. A legend indicates that light blue bars represent “Large model” and dark blue bars represent “Small model,” though the chart does not consistently follow this distinction—some models like Llama 3.1 70B (gray) and phi-4 (dark blue) are labeled outside the legend’s color scheme. The scores range from 66.4 (Llama 3.1 70B) to 91.8 (phi-4), with phi-4 achieving the highest score, followed closely by Gemini Pro 1.5 at 89.8. Most models cluster between 74.8 and 81.6, with phi-4 standing out as the top performer by a significant margin. Error bars are shown atop each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals, though their exact magnitude is not numerically labeled. The chart emphasizes phi-4’s superior performance relative to other contemporary models on this specific benchmark.
